description: Get one news event in detail. A cluster is a single real-world event grouped from the outlets covering it and deduplicated into one item, so you get one event rather than 20 near-duplicate headlines. Returns its summary, a significance score (1 to 10, where 8 and above is exceptional), a source count, the situation it belongs to if any, and links to its source articles (outlet, headline, URL and date). It returns up to 100 of those links, one per outlet; `sources` and `articles_total` are the full count, and `articles_truncated` says whether the list was cut. Use this when the user wants the specifics of one event. Get a cluster id from search_situations, get_situation_timeline, or a clstr.news URL. Results carry canonical clstr.news links. (Requires sign-in, or a free API key: https://clstr.news/developers)

articles.description: How many source articles to return, 1 to 100. Default 100. Lower it when you only need a few citations; the source count is reported separately and is unaffected.

cluster_id.description: Cluster id or slug (from timelines, search, or clstr.news URLs).

name: get_cluster

articles.description: Links to its source articles (outlet, headline, URL and date).

url.description: The outlet's own URL, null when it could not be published.

articles_total.description: How many outlets are behind this event in total. `articles` is capped, this is not.

articles_truncated.description: True when `articles` holds fewer entries than `articles_total`.

merged_into_shown.description: Present when a merged-away event was served as its successor.

significance_score.description: AI-generated significance, 1 to 10, where 8 and above is exceptional.

sources.description: How many outlets are behind this event.

title: Get a news event
